question: How thick is the salt left under the Mediterranean when it dried out?
answer: Under the Mediterranean lies salt 2 to 3 km thick. Drilling in the 1970s dated it to about 5.6 million years ago. Only a sea that dried out could leave that much salt.
move: Under the Mediterranean lies salt 2–3 km thick: proof the sea once dried up.
